process_area.title: Recovery, Disposal, Compliance Reporting & Stewardship Analytics

value_stream.name: Household Hazardous Waste, Paint & Used-Product Stewardship Take-Back Program

fields.Frequency: Per manifest batch; quarterly recovery audit
fields.Participants: TSD Facility, Sustainability/ESG Manager, Internal Audit (VS-21)
fields.Trigger: Manifest arrives at TSD (W5351/W5360); periodic recovery verification

workflows.name: TSD Facility Processing, Recovery, Recycling & Energy-Recovery Verification

Automation Opportunity: - TSD processing confirmation auto-reconciles to the manifest and auto-requests recovery certificates.
Controls: - CTL-793 (ensure controlled execution — Recovery, Disposal, Compliance Reporting & Stewardship Analytics (PA-187.3).)
- operational: cradle-to-grave TSD verification; CTL-21 (quantity reconciliation).
Cross-references: - links to VS-161 (TPRM), VS-21 (audit), VS-88 (records), VS-25 (ESG recovery reporting)
Pain Points / Risks: - **False-recovery risk**: a TSD reports recycling that was actually landfill disposal, undermining ESG claims and cradle-to-grave compliance; mitigated by recovery-certificate verification and quarterly sampling audits.
- **Discrepancy risk**: manifest-out vs. TSD-received quantity gaps indicate leakage/loss; mitigated by per-manifest reconciliation and discrepancy investigation.
System Touchpoints: - Hazardous-waste manifest/chain-of-custody close-out; TSD recovery-certificate register; audit-trail (VS-21/VS-88).
Time Estimate: - ~20 min per manifest close-out; ~10,000/yr → ~3,300 person-hours/yr group-wide.

steps.activity: Receive TSD processing confirmation per manifest: stream, quantity, processing method (recycle/recovery/disposal).
Verify the processing method matches the agreed recovery path (e.g. oil re-refined, batteries recycled, lamps mercury-recovered).
Capture recovery certificates/yields per stream and partner; reconcile to the manifest (cradle-to-grave close).
Audit a sample of TSD records quarterly (internal audit cross-link VS-21).
Flag any discrepancy (short recovery, unexplained disposal) for TPRM follow-up (VS-161).

fields.Participants: Reblending Partner, CSR/Foundation (VS-152), Paint Dept, Pricing (VS-57)
fields.Trigger: Usable latex paint identified at take-back (W5353)

workflows.name: Latex Paint Reblending, Donation-to-Community & Reuse-Product Sales Channel

Automation Opportunity: - Reblended-batch auto-creates a recycled SKU and routes by channel decision rules.
Controls: - CTL-31: NRV/quality provision on recycled stock; CTL-114 (recovery-revenue recognition accuracy).
Cross-references: - links to VS-09 (paint), VS-01 (assortment/SKU), VS-57 (pricing), VS-152 (CSR donation), VS-180 (disaster-relief donation)
Pain Points / Risks: - **QA risk**: reblended paint of inconsistent quality (coverage/odor) erodes brand trust; mitigated by QA before re-sale and clear recycled-product labeling.
- **Mis-pricing risk**: pricing reblended paint above its perceived value leaves it unsold; mitigated by competitive positioning and a donation outlet as alternative.
System Touchpoints: - New recycled-SKU setup (VS-01/VS-29); pricing/merchandising (VS-57); CSR donation records (VS-152); recovery-revenue GL.
Time Estimate: - ~2–4 weeks elapsed per batch cycle; recovery yield ~PHP 50–150/liter vs. disposal cost.

steps.activity: Consolidate usable latex paint at the reblending partner; blend, filter, and standardize into a limited color range.
QA the reblended paint (coverage, adhesion, VOC); label as reblended/recycled product.
Route to the preferred channel: donation to community housing/disaster-recovery (VS-152/VS-180) or sale as a value recycled product.
For sale: price and merchandise as a recycled/reblended SKU (VS-01/VS-57); recognize recovery revenue.
Track recovery revenue and donation value for the program business case (W5368).

fields.Participants: TSD Facility, HSE Officer, Sustainability/ESG Manager
fields.Trigger: Non-recoverable hazardous waste (oil-based paint, contaminated oil, restricted pesticides, etc.)

workflows.name: Hazardous Waste Disposal, Incineration/Cement-Kiln & Landfill Diversion Tracking

Automation Opportunity: - Disposal-method auto-tagged on manifest close-out; diversion-rate auto-computed.
Controls: - CTL-793 (ensure controlled execution — Recovery, Disposal, Compliance Reporting & Stewardship Analytics (PA-187.3).)
Cross-references: - links to VS-179 (EPR/cement-kiln co-processing), VS-25 (ESG), VS-114 (DG disposal), VS-73 (store waste)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Diversion-target risk**: excessive landfill disposal undermines the program's ESG value and diversion targets; mitigated by the recovery hierarchy and diversion-rate tracking.

- **Illegal-disposal risk**: disposal to an unpermitted landfill/incinerator is a RA 6969/RA 9003 violation and cradle-to-grave liability; mitigated by licensed-TSD-only routing and recovery certificates.
System Touchpoints: - Manifest close-out with disposal-method/destination; diversion-rate dashboard (VS-25/VS-28).

steps.activity: Confirm the stream is non-recoverable per the recovery hierarchy (reuse > recycle > energy-recovery > disposal).
Route to the licensed disposal method: cement-kiln co-processing (energy recovery), licensed incineration, or permitted hazardous-waste landfill.
Capture the disposal method and destination for the manifest close-out and diversion tracking.
Track the landfill-diversion rate (diverted vs. landfilled) as a program KPI (W5368).
Minimize disposal over time by improving recovery (W5361/W5362) and assortment/substitution.

fields.Trigger: Monthly/quarterly ledger close; annual DENR-EMB hazardous-waste report cycle

workflows.name: Take-Back Volume Tracking, DENR-EMB Annual Hazardous Waste Report & NSWMC Filing

Automation Opportunity: - DENR-EMB report auto-generated from the reconciled ledger; filing-calendar alerts from the permit portfolio.
Controls: - CTL-793 (ensure controlled execution — Recovery, Disposal, Compliance Reporting & Stewardship Analytics (PA-187.3).)
- operational: statutory environmental reporting; reporting accuracy/reconciliation; .
Cross-references: - links to VS-22 (compliance), VS-179 (EPR/NSWMC), VS-88 (records), VS-25 (ESG), VS-166 (filing calendar)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Reporting-error risk**: an inaccurate DENR-EMB hazardous-waste report is itself a violation (penalties, permit risk); mitigated by ledger→manifest→TSD reconciliation before submission.
- **Deadline-miss risk**: late DENR-EMB/NSWMC filing triggers penalties; mitigated by the permit-portfolio reporting calendar (VS-166) and lead-time.
System Touchpoints: - Hazardous-waste ledger aggregation; DENR-EMB report format; NSWMC/EPR filing (VS-179); records retention (VS-88); ESG reporting (VS-25).
Time Estimate: - ~3 weeks elapsed per annual cycle; ~1 week per monthly close.

steps.activity: Aggregate the hazardous-waste ledger by stream, store, and entity for the reporting period.
Reconcile volumes to manifests and TSD recovery certificates (W5361/W5363).
Prepare the DENR-EMB hazardous-waste generator report (annual) and NSWMC/EPR-aligned filings (cross-link VS-179).
Legal/Finance review; submit via the DENR/NSWMC channels; retain per records-retention (VS-88).
Feed the volumes into ESG/sustainability reporting (VS-25) and program analytics (W5368).

fields.Frequency: Annual internal audit; ad-hoc regulatory inspections
fields.Participants: Compliance Specialist, TPRM (VS-161), Legal (VS-100), HSE Officer
fields.Trigger: Annual audit plan; DENR-EMB/LGU inspection; TSD/transporter accreditation lapse or incident
fields.Volume: ~1 annual audit; ~10–30 regulatory inspections/yr across stores

workflows.name: Product Stewardship Compliance Audit, TPRM of Transporters/TSD & Regulatory Inspection Response

Automation Opportunity: - TSD/transporter accreditation status auto-re-verified from DENR registry at each cycle.
Controls: - CTL-793 (ensure controlled execution — Recovery, Disposal, Compliance Reporting & Stewardship Analytics (PA-187.3).)
- operational: regulatory inspection readiness; CTL-33/CTL-06 (TSD accreditation); internal-audit independence (VS-21).
Cross-references: - links to VS-21 (internal audit), VS-161 (TPRM), VS-22 (compliance), VS-166 (permits), VS-100 (legal)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Inspection-finding risk**: an inspection that finds permit gaps, ledger/manifest mismatches, or unaccredited TSD triggers penalties/closure; mitigated by the annual internal audit and TPRM re-verification.
- **TSD-failure risk**: a TSD losing accreditation mid-contract stockpiles waste at stores; mitigated by TPRM monitoring and backup partners (W5347).
System Touchpoints: - Audit-findings register (VS-21); TPRM inventory (VS-161); permit/manifest evidence (VS-166/VS-88).
Time Estimate: - ~3–4 weeks elapsed per annual audit; ~1–3 days per regulatory inspection.

steps.activity: Audit take-back operations against the program SOP, permits (W5346), and manifest chain-of-custody (W5351).
Re-verify transporter/TSD DENR accreditation and HSSE record (TPRM — VS-161).
On a DENR-EMB/LGU inspection: present permits, ledger, manifests, and recovery certificates; escort inspectors.
Document findings and corrective actions; track to closure (VS-21/VS-22).
Escalate any material finding (permit breach, TSD failure) to the board ESG/risk reporting (VS-25/VS-36).

fields.Frequency: Uncommon (~20–80 incidents/yr group-wide, per the Volume register); high severity
fields.Participants: Store Manager, Compliance Specialist, BFP, DENR-EMB (if reportable), Medical (VS-83)
fields.Trigger: Spill/leak (oil/paint/acid/mercury), battery thermal event, or customer/staff exposure at a take-back point

workflows.name: Take-Back Program Incident, Spill/Leak & Exposure Response

Automation Opportunity: - Incident-report app with substance-specific response checklists and auto-started notice clocks.
Controls: - CTL-793 (ensure controlled execution — Recovery, Disposal, Compliance Reporting & Stewardship Analytics (PA-187.3).)
- operational: spill kits + substance procedures at every point.
Cross-references: - links to VS-24 (HSE), VS-114 (DG incident), VS-26 (insurance), VS-83 (medical/first aid), VS-133 (lessons-learned)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Exposure/escalation risk**: a mishandled mercury or acid spill exposes staff/customers and escalates to a reportable environmental incident; mitigated by substance-specific response procedures and spill kits at every point.
- **Notice-window risk**: late DENR-EMB/BFP/insurance notification compounds the incident; mitigated by an incident-response SLA with defined notice windows.
System Touchpoints: - Incident/case module (VS-24/VS-23); spill-response substance library; insurance/DENR-reportable filing.

steps.activity: Secure the area, contain the spill with the spill kit, and evacuate/exclude customers; render first aid/exposure care.
Identify the substance (mercury, acid, oil, solvent) and apply the substance-specific response (e.g. mercury vapor procedure for broken lamps — W5356).
Notify BFP/DENR-EMB if reportable (significant spill, mercury release, fire); notify insurance (VS-26).
Clean up, dispose of contaminated material via the licensed TSD (W5360), and decontaminate the area.
Root-cause and corrective action (containment design, staff training, policy); capture lessons-learned (VS-133).

fields.Trigger: Monthly co-funding cycle; vendor invoicing for TSD services

workflows.name: Stewardship Program Cost Recovery, Co-Funding Reconciliation & Vendor Settlement

Automation Opportunity: - Co-funding receivable auto-computed from scanned returns; TSD invoices auto-2-way-matched to manifests.
Controls: - CTL-39: co-funding/rebate accuracy; CTL-14/CTL-44 (invoice match); CTL-21 (recovery-revenue accuracy).
Cross-references: - links to VS-15 (P2P/AP), VS-39 (rebates/co-funding), VS-179 (EPR/PRO settlement), VS-17 (GL)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Co-funding-leakage risk**: failing to claim brand co-funding on eligible returns leaves recovery revenue on the table; mitigated by per-brand/SKU reconciliation against returns.
- **Invoice-accuracy risk**: TSD invoices not matched to manifests over-state cost; mitigated by 2-way match (manifest→invoice).
System Touchpoints: - AP/2-way-match (VS-15); co-funding/rebate module (VS-39); recovery-revenue GL; program P&L.
Time Estimate: - ~2 weeks elapsed per monthly cycle; ~20 person-hours.

steps.activity: Reconcile actual take-back volumes (by brand/SKU) against manufacturer co-funding terms (W5348).
Compute co-funding receivable per brand and recovery revenue (reblended paint, scrap metal, battery lead — W5362/W5363).
Process and 2-way-match TSD/transporter vendor invoices against manifests (VS-15).
Settle co-funding receivables with brands and TSD payables; net into the program P&L.
Report program cost-recovery vs. gross cost to the ESG/steering committee (W5368).

fields.Trigger: Monthly/quarterly program-performance review; ESG reporting cycle

workflows.name: Diversion Rate, Recycling Yield, Customer Participation & Program Impact Analytics

Automation Opportunity: - Auto-refreshing diversion/yield/participation dashboard from the reconciled ledger; target-vs-actual auto-flag.
Controls: - CTL-793 (ensure controlled execution — Recovery, Disposal, Compliance Reporting & Stewardship Analytics (PA-187.3).)
Cross-references: - links to VS-25 (ESG reporting), VS-28 (BI), VS-118 (revenue assurance on recovery), VS-36 (board ESG reporting), VS-152 (CSR impact)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Under-performance-blindness risk**: a stream/store under-performing without measurement leaves the program below target and business case; mitigated by monthly metrics with explicit adjust decisions.
- **ESG-claim risk**: reporting diversion/yield metrics not supported by reconciled data (greenwashing); mitigated by ledger→manifest→TSD-reconciled metrics (W5361/W5364).
System Touchpoints: - BI/analytics on the take-back ledger + recovery + customer data (VS-28); ESG reporting module (VS-25).
Time Estimate: - ~1 week per monthly review; ~2 person-hours/week ongoing.

steps.activity: Compute diversion rate (diverted from landfill ÷ total), recycling yield per stream, and recovery revenue vs. cost.
Compute customer participation (unique participants, repeat rate, per-store penetration) and footfall/attach lift.
Compare to diversion targets (W5345) and benchmark; identify under-performing stores/streams.
Feed the metrics into ESG/sustainability reporting and board ESG reporting (VS-25/VS-36).
Recommend program adjustments (scope, incentives, partner mix) to the steering committee (W5345).
